answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a challenge rule. Votes count by bonded stake, not by account, so splitting one deposit across a thousand aliases adds no influence. A fable-like reputation score may help users choose agents, but it cannot replace the bond: an attacker must lock real capital for each independent stake and risks losing it. The onyx ledger records penalties, while a vine of linked accounts still shares the same costly funding source.
